name: Nembi
catalog_citation: Tipton, Ruth A. 1982. Nembi procedural and narrative discourse. Pacific Linguistics B-82. Canberra: Department of Linguistics, Research School of Pacific Studies, Australian National University. vi+92 pp. DOI 10.15144/PL-B82 (CC BY-SA 4.0 online edition).
catalog_locator: Appendix B 'Final verb affixation for person number tense and mode', printed p. 79 = PDF page 85 (heading on printed p. 78 = PDF page 84); file
catalog_quote: Nembi has two phonemic tones: high and low. In the verb charts, second and third person forms which appear to be identical are distinguished by tone. Second person endings have low tone, and third person endings have high. Tone, however, carries a low functional load in the language and is not written. In discourse, the context makes second and third person referents clear, and tone is not marked.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.rule_in_words: The source describes Nembi as having two phonemic tones (high vs. low) with low functional load, exemplified by 2nd- vs 3rd-person verb endings; it says nothing at all about word stress or accent placement.
new_statements.exceptions: None; tone is said to be unwritten and unmarked in the texts.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone statement concerns word-level (verb-suffix) contrasts in a discourse study; it is a four-sentence phonological note, not a phonology description. No statement about stress at word or phrase level.
new_statements.identity_note: Tipton 1982 describes 'Nembi', spoken in the Nembi Valley and on the Nembi Plateau, Southern Highlands Province (Christian Union Mission area, south of the Nipa/Augu = Angal Heneng West zone); Glottolog codes Tipton 1982 to Angal Enen [aoe] = anga1294. Glottolog's only dialect for anga1294 is Megi [megi1246]; Tipton does not name a sub-dialect. Rule 1965, though titled 'Mendi and Nembi Valleys', is coded by Glottolog to Angal [age] and Angal Heneng [akh] (Wela = Augu), so its Nembi-valley data may not be aoe.
